season_calls.rule: At 09:00 on each Hot Season day, AEMO's forecast of the day's highest energy requirement (the pre-dispatch run public by 09:00 that day) is compared with the 4th-highest actual daily maximum of the season so far, less a tolerance learnt from the 2023-24 and 2024-25 Hot Seasons (the q-quantile of how far the forecast fell short). The forecast made at 09:00 the day before is checked the same way against what was known then. If either reaches its threshold, the day is flagged as a possible system peak day and the offer calls a 2-hour event 17:30-19:30 (standby 15:30-17:30) while calls remain under its yearly cap. Until four days of the season are known every day is flagged (threshold null, auto_flag_first_days true). The custom offer uses q = 0.75; the reference terms use q = 0.9 under S2b and q = 0.75 under S3 (each policy's rule was fitted to it on data up to 2026-06-30). The rule never calls on price, and the supply-margin forecast is not used (it failed its pre-set test). Calls are decided at 09:00 with no look-ahead; actual_peak_mw, actual_rank_in_season and ircr_peak_day are known only afterwards.

fields.forecast_peak_mw / threshold_mw: same-day forecast and the custom offer's threshold (q = 0.75), MW
fields.forecast_dayahead_mw / threshold_dayahea: forecast public at 09:00 the day before and its threshold (q = 0.75)
fields.threshold_ref_s2b_*: the reference terms' thresholds under S2b (q = 0.9); under S3 the reference uses the custom thresholds
fields.auto_flag_first_days: a route had fewer than four season days known, so it flagged the day automatically (its threshold is null)
fields.flag_route_*: which forecast reached its threshold: same_day, day_ahead (empty = not flagged)
fields.calls_left_before_*: calls left in the contract-year cap before the day (S2b)
fields.actual_peak_mw: actual daily maximum energy requirement (the quantity the rule forecasts), MW

season_calls.source: Re-run (read-only) of vpp/policy/policy_simulator.py ircr_flags() -> vpp/site_bill.py dynamic_flags(), forecast_tolerance(), peak_day_predictor() (data/processed/spike_table.parquet pd_day_req_max, days_ahead 0 and 1), daily_max(wem_30min.parquet req_energy_mw), and select_calls() with the saved rules; flags equal load_forecasts().flags, call counts and peak-day coverage equal reports/policy/policy_backtest.csv. No saved per-day file existed (customer_kwh_value/out/daily.csv has the custom offer's calls only, without forecast or threshold).

wholesale.label: Wholesale value of the change in the meters' net export (standby charging and rebound included)

capacity.label: Capacity (IRCR) value: lower median meter import in the 12 Peak SWIS intervals x RCP

capacity_share.label: Share of the capacity value passed to Zenith (s = 0.5, assumed TPA term)

pay_energy.label: Customer payment per kWh of event net export

offset.label: Standby offset credit (extra standby import at the retail tariff)

bill.label: Customer's retail bill change (extra imports at 33.26c less DEBS 10c/2c on exports)

receiver_by_scenario.S2b: retailer (Zenith's own retail arm; left out of Zenith's policy profit)

ops_event.label: Zenith operating cost per responding customer per event ($0.05, assumed)

ops_customer.label: Zenith operating cost per enrolled customer ($25/yr, assumed)

fixed.label: Programme fixed cost ($0 in the base case)

wear.label: Customer battery wear ($0.05/kWh extra throughput, assumed)

sign_convention.value_created: aud = value created (may be negative), received by 'receiver'
sign_convention.transfer: aud = amount the payer pays the receiver; creates no value
sign_convention.cost: aud = cost borne by the payer; reduces value created

S2b.retailer_aud: Zenith's own retail arm: the customers' extra retail bill. Its revenue must also pay network charges and fees that are not modelled, so it is kept out of Zenith's policy profit (zenith_aud) - conservative.
S2b.other_aud: 0 by construction: energy and the full capacity value go to Zenith in S2b.

S3.retailer_aud: Synergy as the households' retailer: the customers' extra retail bill.
S3.other_aud: Synergy as market participant and capacity-cost holder: the wholesale value of the change in net export plus the half of the capacity value it does not pass to Zenith.

value_by_party.how_to_read: zenith_aud + customers_aud + retailer_aud + other_aud = value_created_aud for every row. transfers_aud is what Zenith pays customers (payments, fees, offset credits): a transfer, it creates no value. The customers' bill change (customers -> retailer) and, in S3, the capacity share (Synergy -> Zenith) are transfers too (transfers_detail_aud). Every figure is relative to the same batteries in normal self-consumption with no call. Zenith's own 10 MW / 40 MWh site battery is not in these rows and must not be added to them here.

scenarios.S2b: Zenith as retailer of contestable customers under the 2027 Peak IRCR (net export counts negative; companion text, gazetted rules not checked; modelled with the old 4 days x 3 intervals definition). Energy and the full capacity value go to Zenith.
scenarios.S3: Zenith as a Synergy Third Party Aggregator. Energy value stays with Synergy; Zenith receives a share s = 0.5 of the capacity value (assumed: no TPA price exists; break-even s about 31% on the expected year).

value_by_party.enrolment_note: Enrolled homes come from an assumed participation curve (10,000 households offered; half of the maximum 50% enrol at $100/yr expected benefit) and are fractional model outputs, not measured. 0.9 of enrolled batteries are assumed to respond to each call.
value_by_party.source: vpp/policy/policy_simulator.py evaluate_policy() parties, account(), ircr_value() replayed read-only with the saved terms and rules; zenith_aud and customers_aud equal reports/policy/policy_backtest.csv zenith_profit and customer_benefit x enrolled (cases 'B reference', 'C optimised'); retailer_aud + other_aud = the model's 'retailer' party; the four parties sum to the model's 'system' value

inconsistencies.detail: RECOMMENDATION.md:46 says the payment is 'about 85c per kWh of event net export, or the same money as about $8.70 per event'. It is not the same money: the per-event form pays for the nominal 10.25 kWh but billed export averages 7.501 kWh, i.e. about 116.1c per billed kWh (customer_kwh_value RESULTS.md:151). S2b's custom offer uses the per-event form; S3's uses 85c/kWh.

RECOMMENDATION.md:49-50 gives $0.55M (S3) and $2.08M (S2b) 'a year': these are the single contract year 2025-26 backtest. Section 3 gives $0.41M and $1.88M as 'best expected fleet profit': the expected year over three Hot Seasons. Customers: $94 / $145 per enrolled home in 2025-26 vs $126 / $185 expected. Show them with their periods; do not mix.

inconsistencies.topic: Reference call counts depend on the scenario
inconsistencies.detail: 30 / 28 / 27 calls (2023-24 / 2024-25 / 2025-26) hold for the reference under S2b (rule q = 0.9). Under S3 the reference's own fitted rule is q = 0.75 and it calls 30 / 25 / 24 - in 2025-26 the same 24 days as the custom offer. The custom offer calls 42 / 25 / 24 in both scenarios.

inconsistencies.topic: Custom offer covered 3 of 4 peak days in 2025-26
inconsistencies.detail: The custom offer's 24 calls in 2025-26 missed 2026-03-18 (q = 0.75 did not flag it: same-day forecast 3,688 MW against a 3,731 MW threshold); the reference under S2b (q = 0.9, 27 calls) covered all 4. The IRCR reduction is still 3.41 kW per responding home (median of 12 intervals) against 3.42 kW for the reference. RECOMMENDATION.md's '4 of 4' for the custom offer refers to the 2023-24 season only. The missed day, 2026-03-18, is also the day Synergy made its one real activation of the season.

inconsistencies.topic: Holdout vs backtest for the reference in 2023-24
inconsistencies.detail: The reference's 2023-24 result is -$0.28M (S2b) in the leave-one-season-out table but -$311,754 in the backtest: the holdout re-derives enrolment without 2023-24 (1,899 vs 2,234 homes) and charges a full year's operating cost, the backtest 274/365. Different set-ups, not an error.

gaps.reason: The policy study's expected year (Fit in policy_simulator.rule_fits) keeps only Zenith and customer totals; it does not split the retailer, other holders or transfers. The per-season rows above have the full split.

The model gives no forward-looking per-call capacity value at 09:00: the IRCR value is a season-level median over 12 intervals, known only after the season. The kWh-value study's 315c/158c is hindsight (do_not_use).

gaps.reason: A correlated response failure on a peak day (e.g. a communications outage) is not modelled; only an average response of 0.9 (and a 0.5 stress) is.
